title: Verify state machine implementation matches documentation
description:
After implementing enum state machine (lego-radio-cq8), verify the code matches docs/state-machine.md diagrams. Check: 1) All state transitions are correct, 2) Welcome/Playing/Off states behave as documented, 3) Edge cases (wrap-around, first boot) work correctly. Update docs if implementation differs.

## Verification Checklist

**1. State Transitions (see docs/state-machine.md)**
- [ ] Boot → Welcome (automatic on startup)
- [ ] Welcome → Playing(0) (button press)
- [ ] Playing(n) → Playing(n+1) (button press, n < 3)
- [ ] Playing(3) → Off (button press after last channel)
- [ ] Off → Welcome (button press)

**2. Welcome State**
- [ ] Says "Hello!"
- [ ] Says "Checking for updates..."
- [ ] Handles update available/not available
- [ ] Says "Press button to start radio."
- [ ] Waits for button (does NOT auto-advance)

**3. Playing State**
- [ ] Announces channel name (fire-and-forget TTS)
- [ ] Starts stream (ducked 2s, then normal volume)
- [ ] stop() called before new stream

**4. Off State**
- [ ] Stops stream
- [ ] Says "Radio off" (blocking TTS)

**5. Edge Cases**
- [ ] First boot goes to Welcome
- [ ] Wrap-around from Off → Welcome works
- [ ] Rapid button presses are debounced/drained

**6. Documentation Update**
If implementation differs from docs/state-machine.md, update the docs to match.

title: Remove redundant player.stop() call in channel switch
description:
In run_radio(), channel switch calls player.stop() then player.play_stream() which internally calls stop() again. Remove the redundant first stop() call.

## Implementation

**File:** src/main.rs
**Location:** Lines 168-180, the channel playing branch

**Change:** Remove line 173:
```rust
// REMOVE THIS LINE:
player.stop();
```

The play_stream() method at line 176 already calls self.stop() internally (see audio.rs:122).

**Before:**
```rust
player.stop();  // REDUNDANT - remove this
player.speak(channel.tts_name, &tts);
if let Err(e) = player.play_stream(channel.url) {
```

**After:**
```rust
player.speak(channel.tts_name, &tts);
if let Err(e) = player.play_stream(channel.url) {
```

**Testing:** cargo run, switch channels, verify no audio glitches

title: Fix duck timing for slow TTS synthesis on Raspberry Pi
description:
## Problem

On Raspberry Pi, Piper TTS synthesis takes 1-2 seconds. Current flow:

1. `speak()` called → `start_duck()` sets `duck_until = now + 1500ms`
2. Thread spawns → `tts.synthesize()` blocks for 1-2s
3. After synthesis → TTS audio plays

If synthesis takes 1500ms, the duck period expires BEFORE TTS audio starts.
Result: Channel announcements drowned out by stream.

## Solution

Move `start_duck()` call to AFTER `tts.synthesize()` completes, right before audio plays.

## Files to modify

- `src/audio.rs`: Pass `duck_until_ms` and `boot_time` to TTS thread, call `start_duck()` after synthesis

## Testing

Test on actual Pi hardware - verify TTS is audible over ducked stream.
